note: Track legato (guitar-techniques), step 2: the trill with fingers 1 and 3 (legato-trill at level beginner), high on the neck, lower where the reach is wider, then faster in stages.

exercise.title: Hammer-ons and pull-offs, fingers 1 and 3
exercise.why: Fingers 1 and 3 have a fret between them, so finger 3 has further to fall than finger 2 did, and the trill trains it to land on its fret while finger 1 stays down.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome and follow the tab. Pick the first note once, then hammer finger 3 on and pull it off, one note per beat, with no more picking. Finger 1 stays down the whole time.
Keep going until both notes are equally loud.

Press Play below to start the metronome. The trill is now lower on the neck, where the frets are further apart, so finger 3 has to reach.
If finger 3 lands short of its fret, move your thumb along the back of the neck until it reaches.
_Stop and shake out your hand when it aches._

Press Play below to start the metronome and play the trill on the B string.
When both notes are equally loud, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If a note goes missing at a new stage, go back one stage.
